heading: De Officiis, Book I, §§ 53–58 · The degrees of human fellowship (chapters 17–18) · I.53 … I.58

items.text: Honor and keep the marriage bond as the first bond of human society.
items.quote: the first bond of union is that between husband and wife

items.text: Provide all needful material assistance to your children and whole family; they look to you alone for support and protection.
items.quote: next come children and the whole family, who look to us alone for support and can have no other protection

items.text: Repay your parents: their services have laid you under the heaviest obligation after your country.
items.quote: parents; for their services have laid us under the heaviest obligation

items.text: Hold fast to your brothers and sisters in good will and affection.
items.quote: The bonds of common blood hold men fast through good-will and affection

items.text: Give needful material assistance to your kinsmen, whose lot is for the most part one with yours.
items.quote: finally, our kinsmen, with whom we live on good terms and with whom, for the most part, our lot is one

items.text: Hold in common the family traditions, forms of domestic worship, and ancestral tombs.
items.quote: it means much to share in common the same family traditions, the same forms of domestic worship, and the same ancestral tombs
items.conflict: Pagan domestic worship of household spirits or ancestors; worship belongs to God alone.

items.text: Hold one home with all things in common.
items.quote: then we find one home, with everything in common
